items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1962-01-04
items.q: Were you playing regular with Wooden D uppterville? ... Yeah, we had no ride. ... It seemed more of a band out of the same little team. You'd played together before.

ctx.x: Yeah. What band was that? I don't know what he called his band. He called his band a chameleon. Yeah. You were with him back then, huh, sometimes? But not regular. I just wondered how you happened to make the records with him. I really was curious about it. Oh, the records? Oh, that was Bill's idea. That was Bill Russell's idea. How did Bill get connected with you? Uh, well, Bill had seen me and had heard me and never spoke to me, you know, because I was recording or anything like that. But, uh, happened at, I…
Yeah. Yeah. Mm-hm. No, I don't. Were you playing regular with Wooden D uppterville? Mm-hm. Mm-hm.

Yeah, we had no ride. How'd you do it? Just the same as we did with the others at John's Unyall. Just walking cold, huh? Yeah. Well, I guess you knew each other. Yeah. It seemed more of a band out of the same little team. You'd played together before. I wanted to get back to your addresses. You lived in the 2100 block of Allen Street? The 2,100. 2,100? Mm-hmm. And you were just a young kid. I was just a kid. And how were you before you moved away from that? Oh, I must have been around about 9 or 10. And then…
